# X6 R304 — fast exact suffix continuation after R303

2026-11-28. Independent informed TASK_RESEARCH, NOT_REVIEWED. Predecessor 2ee44c658f3158a3fff5ca1bac8e6d29bf0545d2:research_notes/portable_direct/2026-11-28_r2_x6_r303_monotone_suffix_core_propagation.md, blob 329296935bee21c747147ceaa2878688b8abb5d0. Same native read, frozen science, P000 V4/V5, ACTIVE worldview, and scope as R303. No shared state mutation; own identity and Activity binding unconfirmed.

R303 proved hereditary failure, but spent 4,909,269 of 5,000,000 recursive split checks on greedy core shrinkage, yielding only 67 propagated rejections. For this residual segment use the verified R303 cores (subset antichain), turn off shrinkage, and preserve each newly failed full branch as a reusable core. Exact memo hits are tested before new work. This is a method change, not a change to the mathematical predicate.

The label lookup is optimized without changing its output. Decompose an unsigned 98-bit germ mask into words of widths 32,32,34 (the high word fits exactly in a JS Number). For final 14-bit block, use exact integer floor division by 2^20 rather than the JavaScript unsigned 32-bit right shift, which discards the top two bits. The first trial using the latter failed the one-bit cross-check before classification; it was corrected, with no results counted from that trial. A second attempt stopped before classification because a parser matched a heading string within the predecessor code; the corrected parser anchors actual heading lines. Each block remains the same consecutive 14-bit section as R302; equivalence follows from shifts and masks. The actual reproducer checks all 98 one-bit masks and 4,096 full-width deterministic masks against the original block implementation, as well as sampled brute conditioned label counts. The raw carrier and zero semantics remain unchanged.
